faq.q: What is the origin of Sani?
faq.a: Sani is associated with Arabic. Sani is the Hausa form of Arabic ثَانِي (Thānī), meaning 'second'.
Yes — the underlying form ثَانِي is Arabic.
Sani can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sani should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Thānī is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sani mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Sani mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sani is rendered ثانی and carries the sense ثانی، دوم.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-ni. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sani?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sani, sani. Script forms are ثاني, ثانی, ثَانِي, सानी.

faq.q: Is Sani a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
